API Reference

This section summarizes the main Python modules and HTTP endpoints that make up RAPAS Photometry Pipeline. The project is primarily used through the Streamlit frontend, but several modules and backend routes are also useful for programmatic access.

Application Modules

Frontend and UI

pages/app.py

Main Streamlit workflow for FITS upload, parameter selection, astrometry, photometry, cross-matching, result export, and transient finding.

pages/login.py

Login, registration, password recovery, and backend selection workflow. Every successful sign-in is written to the Streamlit log as [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] RPP vX.Y.Z - User '<username>' logged in successfully (frontend, <backend> backend).

pages/api_client.py

Thin HTTP client used by the Streamlit frontend to talk to the FastAPI backend. Includes backend auto-detection logic.

Science and Processing Modules

src/pipeline.py

Core photometry helpers including masking, cosmic-ray handling, and other lower-level processing helpers. It also owns the effective-gain resolution (resolve_effective_gain / instrument_uses_driver_gain) shared by the error model, the cosmic-ray mask and SEP detection: explicit EGAIN, CCDGAIN and CVF (gain = 1/CVF) keywords take precedence over the conventional GAIN, which is ignored on recognised driver-gain cameras (QHY/ZWO) because it is an abstract driver setting rather than e-/ADU.

src/astrometry.py

Plate solving and WCS-related utilities using stdpipe and local Astrometry.net tooling.

src/psf.py

PSF photometry helpers and PSF model construction, including the empirical PSF (ePSF) builder and compute_encircled_energy for the aperture correction.

src/xmatch_catalogs.py

Catalog cross-matching and catalog enhancement, including GAIA, SIMBAD, SkyBoT, and related services.

src/transient.py

Transient candidate search, reference-survey/catalog comparison, and extra filtering such as Solar System object rejection.

src/tools_pipeline.py

Shared photometry and WCS utilities such as filter mapping, pixel scale extraction, background estimation, and calibrated magnitude helpers.

src/pipeline.py also exposes check_psf_aperture_consistency(), which matches PSF and aperture sources by position and reports the median psf_mag - aperture_mag per aperture, warning when the offset exceeds PSF_APERTURE_CONSISTENCY_THRESHOLD (0.15 mag). Diagnostics are stored in st.session_state["psf_aperture_consistency"], and add_calibrated_magnitudes exports the per-source difference as psf_minus_aperture_mag_X_X (with filter-prefixed aliases, NaN where only one method measured the source).

src/tools_app.py

Streamlit-side helper functions including FITS loading, cache reset, and UI support routines. plot_photometry_offsets() renders the per-source psf_mag - aperture_mag offset (scatter against calibrated PSF magnitude with per-aperture median/zero lines, plus the histogram) shown in the results view.

Database and API Modules

api/main.py

FastAPI application with health, authentication, config persistence, and FITS upload/listing endpoints. A successful POST /api/login writes [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] RPP vX.Y.Z - User '<username>' logged in successfully (FastAPI backend). to the service log; the legacy backend (backend.py) emits the same line tagged (legacy backend).

api/models.py

SQLAlchemy ORM models for users, FITS storage, recovery codes, and tracking tables.

api/schemas.py

Pydantic request and response models for the FastAPI service.

api/storage.py

Storage path generation for uploaded FITS files and related backend storage conventions.

Useful Functions

src.tools_app.load_fits_data(file)

Load image data and headers from a FITS file with robust handling for empty, invalid, multi-extension, or multi-dimensional FITS content.

src.tools_app.update_observatory_from_fits_header(header)

Extract observatory metadata (name, latitude, longitude, elevation) from a FITS header and update the Streamlit session state observatory fields.

src.tools_app.display_archived_files_browser(api_client)

Render the archived FITS file and ZIP result browser in the Streamlit sidebar. Queries the backend for the current user’s stored files.

src.tools_pipeline.safe_wcs_create(header)

Attempt to build a WCS object from a FITS header while returning structured error information and log messages.

src.tools_pipeline.extract_pixel_scale(header)

Extract or estimate the pixel scale used by later photometric and astrometric steps.

src.pipeline.make_border_mask(image, border=50, invert=True, dtype=bool)

Build a border mask for detection workflows.

src.pipeline.fwhm_fit(image, objects, pixel_scale)

Estimate the FWHM of the stellar PSF by fitting Gaussian profiles to detected sources and averaging the results with sigma clipping.

src.pipeline.detect_and_mask_satellite_trails(image_data, header, temp_fits_path=None)

Detect satellite trails in an image using ASTRiDE and return a boolean mask with trail pixels set to True. Returns an empty mask when ASTRiDE is unavailable or no trails are found.

src.pipeline.show_subtracted_image(image_sub)

Display the background-subtracted image inside the Streamlit interface.

src.astrometry.solve_with_astrometrynet(file_path)

Run local astrometric solving with the configured Astrometry.net/stdpipe stack.

src.xmatch_catalogs.cross_match_with_gaia(...)

Cross-match measured sources with calibration catalogs and prepare data for zero-point estimation and later enrichment.

src.xmatch_catalogs.enhance_catalog(...)

Enrich the photometry catalog with additional catalog matches such as SIMBAD, SkyBoT, and Astro-Colibri.

src.transient.find_candidates(...)

Run the transient candidate workflow after photometry and catalog preparation. Sources are detected with SExtractor, unreliable detections are dropped using the SEP flag mask (SEP_REJECT_FLAGS) and matched to the photometry catalog within a seeing-based radius, and reference-survey / Vizier matches are rejected unless the detection is a genuine brightness excess (mag_threshold, default 2.0 mag). No minimum S/N cutoff is applied; low-S/N detections can remain candidates if they pass the other catalog and known-object filters.

Photometric Formula Conventions

The project documentation and code use the following formulas consistently:

  • σ_flux² = σ_aperture² + σ_total_bkg² + σ_centroid² (aperture-sum error, the local-background error from the sigma-clipped annulus, and the centroid-position term)

  • σ_bkg_pixel = ApertureStats.median_err = √(π/2) · s / √A_ann (standard error of the median annulus level)

  • S/N = flux / flux_error (computed from the background-subtracted, aperture-corrected flux)

  • σ_mag = 1.0857 × (σ_flux / flux), combined in quadrature with the aperture-correction systematic σ_apcorr = 1.0857 · f_apcorr · |apcorr − 1| / apcorr

  • flux_total = flux_aperture / EE(r) (encircled-energy aperture correction)

  • σ_mag_calib = √(σ_mag_inst² + σ_zp² + σ_sys²), where σ_zp uses the sigma-clipped, untrimmed residual scatter and the √(π/2) median factor

Photometry Error Columns

The exported photometry catalog exposes the error budget explicitly so it can be inspected or recombined downstream:

  • background_rms_per_pixel_X_X — local-background median_err per pixel

  • centroid_flux_err_X_X — centroid-position term

  • apcorr_X_X / ee_fraction_X_X — aperture correction and its encircled-energy fraction

  • apcorr_mag_err_X_X — aperture-correction magnitude systematic

  • aperture_mag_err_X_X / psf_mag_err — total calibrated magnitude error (after zero-point propagation)

  • aperture_mag_err_X_X_random / ..._correlated and psf_mag_err_random / psf_mag_err_correlated — the per-source and field-common components of the calibrated magnitude error

  • aperture_mag_X_X_colorcorr_err / psf_mag_colorcorr_err — errors of the color-term-corrected magnitudes

  • zero_point_std — field-level formal zero-point uncertainty

The total aperture flux error (aperture + local background + centroid) is computed as the aperture_sum_bkg_corr_err_X_X column by detection_and_photometry; it is an intermediate quantity that add_calibrated_magnitudes does not retain in the exported catalog. The calibrator scatter and count diagnostics (zero_point_scatter, zero_point_scatter_kept, zero_point_n) are stored on the matched calibration table used for zero-point diagnostics, not on the exported source catalog.

Analysis Result Files

The Streamlit workflow writes files to a per-user *_results/ directory. Both ZIP builders include files matching the input base name except files with the .fits extension. FITS products therefore remain on disk and are not part of the downloadable archive.

HTTP API Endpoints

The FastAPI backend in api/main.py currently exposes these primary routes:

  • GET /health

  • POST /api/register

  • POST /api/login

  • POST /api/recovery/request

  • POST /api/recovery/confirm

  • GET /api/config

  • POST /api/config

  • POST /api/upload/fits

  • GET /api/fits

The optional legacy Flask backend in backend.py exposes an equivalent configuration surface for older deployments (see api.rst for the full persistence comparison):

  • POST /register

  • POST /login

  • POST /recover_request

  • POST /recover_confirm

  • POST /save_config

  • GET /get_config

Maintenance and Migration Scripts

The repository also contains command-line helpers in scripts/:

  • scripts/migrate_add_wcs_zip_tables.py

  • scripts/migrate_legacy_db.py

  • scripts/satellite_trail_detector.py

These are maintenance or standalone utilities and are not all part of the main interactive Streamlit workflow.

Test Suite

Tests live in tests/ and run with pytest from the project root. The modules most relevant to backend and settings behaviour are:

  • tests/test_config_persistence.py — FastAPI and legacy Flask configuration round-trips, default seeding of mag_err_max / effective_gain, and the save/load wiring in pages/app.py and pages/login.py

  • tests/test_robustness_ingestion.py — FastAPI FITS ingestion and listing

  • tests/test_database.py — ORM models and analysis-history tracking

  • tests/test_photometry.py — photometry and error-budget calculations, including the PSF star-selection regression, the ePSF centring, the PSF-vs-aperture consistency diagnostic and the effective-gain resolution (CVF inversion, keyword precedence, driver-camera detection and the plausible range)

  • tests/test_version_consistency.py — release-version agreement across pyproject.toml, src/__version__.py, docs/conf.py, the README and the changelog
